purpose: Praziquantel is used to treat infections caused by certain parasitic worms, including tapeworms and blood flukes (schistosomes). It helps your body get rid of these unwanted parasites. Your doctor may prescribe it if you have been exposed to contaminated water or food in certain parts of the world.
how_it_works: Praziquantel works by causing the worm's muscles to cramp and spasm, which paralyzes the worm. It also damages the outer skin of the worm, making it easier for your immune system to attack and destroy it. The dead or dying worms are then passed out of your body naturally.
common_side_effects: You may feel dizzy, drowsy, or have a headache after taking this medication. Nausea, stomach pain, and feeling generally unwell are also common. These side effects are usually mild and go away on their own within a day or two.
warnings: Do not drive or operate heavy machinery right after taking this medicine because it can make you feel dizzy or drowsy. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, as the dose may need to be adjusted. Avoid taking it with rifampin (an antibiotic) as it can make praziquantel much less effective. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medication.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on the type of worm infection you have. It is usually taken as one to three doses in a single day, with each dose taken 4 to 6 hours apart. Tablets should be swallowed whole with water during a meal — do not chew them because they taste very bitter. Always follow exactly what your doctor tells you.
